turns.content: Let f and g map the positive integers to themselves and satisfy g^{g(n)+1}(n)+g^{f(n)}(n)=f(n+1)-g(n+1)+1 for every n, where superscripts denote iterates. Derive the strict inequality involving f^{g(n)+1}(n) and f(n+1).
Let y_1 be the least value attained by f. Use the strict inequality to determine every positive integer x for which f(x)=y_1.

List the distinct image values as y_1<y_2<... . Let Q_j mean that f(x)=y_j exactly when x=j, and also let Q_j mean y_j=j. Assuming Q_1,...,Q_n in the first sense and Q_1,...,Q_{n-1} in the second, explain why y_{n+1} exists.
Choose x with f(x)=y_{n+1}. Apply the strict inequality at x-1 and set b=f^{g(x-1)}(x-1). Show that b lies in {1,...,n}, then use the established preimage facts to rule out b<n.
From b=n, prove Q_n and then peel back the iterates using the unique-preimage facts to obtain x=n+1. Explain how this establishes P_{n+1}.
Combine the base case and induction step to determine f on every positive integer.
Substitute that function into the original equation. What relation remains for g, and what does positivity force g(n) to be for every n?
Verify the resulting pair directly in the original functional equation.

Why does the induction also establish that the ordered image values continue indefinitely, rather than assuming in advance that the image of f is infinite? Use this to close the exhaustiveness argument.
State all pairs (f,g) satisfying the equation on the positive integers.
